doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: One-line views of Monk and Duke Ellington
summary: He calls both mavericks who marched to their own drums.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Before we get to the end of our interview, there are several other areas I'd like to cover. The first is just to get your comments and reminiscences about of several other musicians, some of whom you may not have worked with but some of whom I know that you knew. For example, Thelonious Monk.
A maverick who marched to the beat of his own drum and who was a true trailblazer in the evolution of jazz. One of a kind.

. . . who marched to the beat of his own drum and heard, listened to his own inner voices. And whose music was uniquely – it had Duke’s personal touch [in] that you heard just a few seconds of it [and] you knew immediately that that’s Duke Ellington. Couldn’t be anybody but Duke Ellington and sure enough, it wasn’t anybody but Duke
